newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan farmers start grain, oilseed planting.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan farmers start grain, oilseed planting.

text.p: Saskatchewan farmers have started planting grains and oilseeds in the southwest part of the province, although less than one percent of the land had been seeded as of Sunday, Saskatchewan Agriculture said in its weekly crop report.

"The southwest part of the province reports the most planting with some cereal grains and oilseeds seeded. In other areas of the province, the limited planting activity mainly involved the seeding of field peas," the report said.
The report said unsettled weather continued to delay fieldwork, particularly in east central and northern areas.
Crop land topsoil moisture conditions were reported as good to excessive across most of the grain belt.
"Warm, drying conditions are needed in the areas of excessive moisture before spring seeding can begin," the report said.

Combining of the 1996 unharvested crop was under way in the southeast, southwest and central regions of the grain belt. Northern and eastern areas continued to wait for the land to dry up enough to move combines into the fields.
